answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by tying reputation to a public, costly history: every completed job is logged like a vine growing along a trellis, visible to all, and cannot be faked overnight. A new identity starts with no quartz-clear record, so it cannot claim the trust of an orchard that took seasons to cultivate. Creating many fake agents does not copy that history; each must still do real, verifiable work, and the cost of faking it across many identities exceeds any reward from gaming the system.
